correctness.rationale: For Delta>=2, no disjoint TOIDS exist, so the coalition graph has pairwise-intersecting edges and a universal hub. Every partner of a hub failing total domination must meet a fixed neighborhood of size <=Delta; otherwise it meets one of two endpoints of a fixed uncovered edge. Thus k<=Delta+1. Given the independent neighborhood and distance-two condition, X=V\N(v) fails total domination only at v; each singleton w in N(v) repairs this and leaves independent complement N(v)\{w}. This constructs Delta+1 parts. Girth>=5 and delta>=2 imply the local condition by excluding triangles and squares. A standalone exhaustive solver confirms all eligible graph edge masks to order 6 and selected larger exact cases; the unrestricted proof does not rely on enumeration. The six-vertex boundary uses complete Bell(6)=203 partition enumeration.

value.rationale: The defining paper explicitly asks for bounds in minimum and maximum degree. This proves its natural global Delta+1 upper bound is always attained on the entire high-girth delta>=2 class, including irregular and disconnected graphs of unbounded order/degree. It constructs optimal partitions from one neighborhood, rather than merely producing a numerical limit. The girth-four bipartite boundary shows the threshold has genuine content, and the local criterion extends to graph families with four-cycles such as hypercubes.
